title: Grade 6 Math — Tue, Jun 10
description: Basic Geometry — Day 2 of 5: Angles — parts, types and measurement
subject: mathematics

questions.question: An angle is formed by ___.
options: Two rays with a common endpoint
questions.explanation: An angle is formed when two rays share the same starting point (vertex).

questions.question: The common endpoint of the two rays that form an angle is called the ___.
questions.explanation: The shared starting point is called the vertex of the angle.

questions.question: An angle less than 90° is called ___.
An angle exactly equal to 90° is called ___.
questions.explanation: A right angle is exactly 90° — like the corner of a square.

questions.question: An angle greater than 90° but less than 180° is called ___.
An angle of exactly 180° is called ___.
questions.explanation: A straight angle is 180° — it forms a straight line.

questions.question: An angle greater than 180° but less than 360° is called ___.
questions.explanation: A reflex angle is more than 180° but less than 360°.

questions.question: An angle of 360° is called ___.
questions.explanation: 360° is a complete angle — one full rotation.

questions.question: Which type of angle does the letter 'L' look like?
questions.explanation: The letter L has two lines meeting at exactly 90° — a right angle.

questions.question: A clock shows 3:00. The angle between the hands is ___.
questions.explanation: At 3:00, the hour hand points to 3 and minute hand to 12. The angle between them is exactly 90°.

questions.question: What instrument is used to measure angles?
questions.explanation: A protractor is used to measure angles in degrees.

questions.question: An angle of 35° is ___.
questions.explanation: 35° < 90°, so it is an acute angle.

questions.question: An angle of 125° is ___.
questions.explanation: 125° is between 90° and 180°, so it is an obtuse angle.

questions.question: How many degrees are in a right angle?
The arms of an angle are its ___.
options: Two sides of a line segment
questions.explanation: The two rays that form an angle are called its arms (sides).
